div.p: When network mode changes, the transition time analysis of the network is especially important, as there should be no buffer overload and all switches schedulable. To ensure the schedulability of each switch, transition time of the network is needed to analysis. In this paper we provide a method to solve the overload. An offset is introduced, it can be calculate through the windows. After several iterations we will get an feasible offset. However, the introduce of the offset could make no message lose, but it causes a delay of the transition time.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Nowadays, the complexity of the data transmitted in the network increases dramatically. That means data could be transmitted in different types due to satisfy the control performance. For example, during the fly in the air, the plane always expiries several work modes. When planes are taking off or landing, Fly Control System (FCS) needs more accurate in height than planes are cruising. Each work mode has different require for the transmitted data, then it is an unstable factor when planes from one work mode to another work modes. There will be two modes data in the network and no literature analysis such problem in the network. This paper emphasis on no message lose and the network schedulability when work mode change in AFDX network.

AFDX (Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet) is highspeed data transfer network in avionic system. It has a strong require in deterministic. And in ARINC 664, network deterministic means all packets delay could be limited in an upper bound. Then it generates an advantage environment to research about the mode change. Moreover, the network is deterministic with the latency for each connection known in advance. The traffic flow and shaping mechanisms help guarantee the latency, jitter, and bandwidth for each link, providing the QoS required for avionics systems [1].

However, since AFDX is a deterministic network, and [2] [3] [4] has calculated the upper bound of end to end delay, but there is no literature talk about the upper bound of the transition time when work mode changes. And that will bring a new problem with the network topology: each switch gets an input data from other switch or End System, the transition time could be add to the next switch. So it is significance to research for the mode change in AFDX network. In order to solve this problem, we propose a method with windows.

div.head: II. RELATED WORKS
div.p: Most of the literatures are talks about the mode change in Real time system. In [Schedulability analysis for mode changes in [5] offset is introduced to handle the overload transition. A reliable methods has been given in [6], the author proves its applicability by analyzing a case with FP an EDF scheduling. In [7] and [8], Jorge concludes several mode change protocols when work mode changes in RTS, and he proposes a new protocol by combining two methods. However, he does a good job in calculating the offset. [9] provide a automation to describe the modes state when modes change in real-time system.In [11], the author model the AFDX network and [10] gives the worst case response time in AFDX, which lead a way to calculate worst case in mode change.

The rest of the paper is organized as follow: In section 2, we will discuss the system model and the definition of the mode change; in section 3, the primary problem will be point out; and the solution will be given in section 4; the section 5 is talked about the simulation, which will compare the result to the result without protocol; a brief conclusion will be seen in section 6.

div.head: A. Motivation example
div.p: In real time system, several parameters could change when work mode changes. There will be problem during the mode changes; an overload could happen Fig. 1. The Fig. 1 shows the worst case, that is all new mode tasks release at the moment mode changes. We always add an offset to the new mode task. An offset is the delay to the release of the first new mode task in order to reduce the overload produced by mode change. Transition time is considered as the time interval between the mode-change occurs and the There is a simple network with three switches. Suppose ES1 (End-System) and ES2 work mode changes, they send their new data to SW1 (Switch) and SW2 at the same time T1. T1 is the time network mode change starts, so are SW1 and SW2. But the start of SW3's mode change is later than SW1 and SW2. When new message cross the SW2 and arrive at the SW3, it is the time SW3's mode change begins. Until all old messages of SW1 and SW2 finished transmitting, there are all new mode messages in whole network, at which moment, it's the time network finished mode changing. The network's transition time is composed of transition times of SW1, SW2, and SW3. And the transition time of SW1, SW2 and SW3 is crossed with each other. For each SW, there is a scheduler on each output port. Similarly, different schedulers on the same switch have different transition time. The whole transition (network transition) could be divided to switch transition and the switch transition could be divided to scheduler transition. When network mode changes, the transition time analysis of the network is especially important, as there should be no buffer overload and all switches schedulable. To ensure the schedulability of each switch, all transition time of the network is needed to analysis. In order to analysis the network transition time, according to the example, the whole transition time could be divided and conquered.

div.head: B. Problem formulation
div.p: In network the situation is same. There are new messages and old messages while the mode change occurs. The latency of the network mode change is defined as the time interval between the first arrive of the new mode message and the completion of the last/final old message transmits. For consistency, the latency is considered as the transition time. However, the network is combined with several switches, all switches transition time build the network transition. For each switch, transition is different from others.

In order to analysis the network transition time, according to the example, the whole transition time could be divided and conquered. For scheduler, the mode change is as similar as single CPU schedule. However, AFDX allow no packet loss, and then the scheduler should use non-preemptive schedule policy. AFDX is a deterministic network, and all VLs should be configured at design phase. When work mode changes, VLs can't be added dynamic. And the output port scheduler could be designed to adapt all VLs cross the port. Then the output-port scheduler should be powerful enough, however in engineering 24 output-port schedulers on one switch share one CPU. So resource could be saved by scheduling work mode messages, and consume zero resource to deal with the other mode messages.

div.head: A. Mode change definition
div.p: Work mode changes in network is caused by the application layer's mode change, which means the network mode won't change until the application layer has been changed. When the application has change the work mode, then data waiting for transmitting will enter the network. We define the mode change begins when the first changed frame enter the switch network.

In network, messages type could change from one work mode to another work mode, such as maximum length of the virtual link, period of the frame, priority and deadline. When work mode changes, some parameters such like VLs' period could change and there will some new VLs enter the network or leave the network. The new VLs are belong to the new work mode and beyond the old work mode, and they all should be designed at design phase. The finished VLs exists in old mode and are excluded in new mode. We divide all messages into four types: old-mode finished messages, new-mode start messages, changed messages and unchanged messages.

Old-mode finished messages are these virtual links belong to the old-mode network, and do not exist in new-mode network. They should finish their transmit during the mode-change transition, and never received when mode-change occur.
New-mode start messages are these virtual links start to transmit in new-mode network, and do not exist in old-mode network. When mode-change occur, they could start their transmit.

Changed messages are messages exist in both old-and newmode network, some parameters of them get changing, such as priority, period and L max . Before the instance mode-change occur messages arrive with old-mode parameters, and after the instance, messages with changed parameter could be received.
Unchanged messages is opposing to changed messages, they also exist in both old-and new-mode network, and they changed no parameter when mode changed.

div.head: B. Network Model
div.p: AFDX network is a deterministic Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet, which contains End Systems(ES) and Switches. End system receives a variety of data from upper level such as avionic equipment, and sends them to a destination end system through a series of switches.

Each ES put varied data into different virtual links according to the destination end system. Virtual link vl could identify a data flow. Each vl is defined a connection from source ES to one or more destination ES according to static routing tables in switches. vl is determined by two main parameters: BAG and L max . BAG is the minimum transmit interval between the starting bits of two frames of one virtual link.L max is the maximum frame size for virtual link i, which can be configurable ranging from 84bytes to 1538bytes. AFDX switch use store-forward fabric, they receives virtual link data from input port and store them into buffers. When a frame is completely received, switch could forward it to each port buffers according to the static routing table. And scheduler of output could use different scheduling policies to output arrival data.

div.head: V. ANALYSIS METHOD WITH TEMPORAL WINDOW
A. Window Calculate in Single Hop
div.p: Worst case response time is a sufficient analysis to determine if the message transition is failed. To obtain the worstcase response times of the different messages, the messages could be differentiate between old-mode message, changed message, and unchanged messages. To account for the WCRT, a temporal window is introduced. For an old-mode message τ, a temporal window W τ is defined, starting at the receiving of τ before the mode changes and finishing when τ completes sending. And mode-change is supposed to occur x time units after the messages receiving. Therefore, the duration of W τ is a function of x. In order to reduce the overload of the mode change, an offset is used to delay the new messages received. old-mode messages have higher priority than message τ. After the mode-change, no more old-mode message received, and new-mode messages have been received. P om i is the BAG of the old mode VL i. BAG is the minimum interval of two frame in one virtual link. To obtain the worst case, BAG could be considered as the period of the virtual link message. N om hp could be considered as how many higher priority messages arrived at the interval between messages τ arrive and mode changes.
Consider the time slice W τx,

Note that, if a message changes nothing during the modechange transition, we can give it a offset O unchanged = 0. Then mode-change makes no impact on unchanged message. When we compute the message received after mode-change, the unchanged message can be considered as changed message with changing no parameters.

div.head: B. Window Calculate in Multi-Hop
div.p: In single hop, the input of the switch is end system, but a real network is usually composed by multi-hop. It means the switches should be connect with each other. A delay is introduceed when a virtual link from a end system arrive at the second switch of its routing. Then the mode-change on second switch have a delay relative to the first switch.

So, there are different cases in multi-hop scheduling. When mode-change occurs, schedulers on different hops get different transition time. Look at the figure (network and transition), ES3 begin its transition later than ES1 and ES2. ES2's transition could be crossover the ES3's transition.

The situation could be considered as the parameters of several messages changes during the transition. Suppose the topology is considered by figure (network and transition). ES1 and ES2 change their work mode at the same time, transition on SW1 could be consider as one single hop scheduling. But on the SW2, it could be divided into two cases below:

Case1, when new-mode messages of SW1 arrive at SW2, SW2 has finished transition caused by new-mode messages from ES2. Then, the mode change could be considered divided. Transition on SW2 can be partition into two independence phases. One is the transition caused by new-mode message from ES2, and the other is caused by new messages from SW1. The first phase could be considered as one single hop scheduling, and the second phase could be analysis as the messages from ES2 are unchanged.

Case2, when SW2 is in the transition caused by ES2, the new messages of SW1 arrive. Suppose, new-mode messages of SW1 arrive at y time units after mode-change occur at SW2 caused by ES2. We can calculus how many messages have finished mode changes. The worst case response time is still a method to analysis the transition mixed-up by transition caused by SW1 and ES2.

Then the whole transition on SW2 of case 2 can be partition into two independence phases. One is the transition caused by the new-mode messages from ES2, and Y time later, the newmode messages on SW1 cause the second phase.
In the first phase, a temporal window could be calculus follow the equation (3).
For old-mode message τ on switch n of the first phase, according to the Equation ( 3), the window W τ,n :

But in the second transition phase, in order to analysis the process of the parameters changing during the mode change, Y is introduced. Y is a interval between the start of the first phase and second phase, playing a role to remember how many new-mode messages have finished changing. If Y ≥ O i,n , we could say the new-mode messages from the ES2 has finished the transition. For old-mode message, if Y≥Deadline, it has finished transition. If the WCRT is smaller than relative deadline, there will no overload when work mode changes.

div.head: VI. SIMULATION AND ANALYSIS
div.p: In this section, we set up simulations for AFDX network based on truetime, then mode change transition will be given over this network.

div.head: A. Simulation Set Up
div.p: The AFDX network includes 4 switches and 10 end systems, the system architecture is shown in Fig5. Each switch could forward the frame according to route tables. VLs includes send time, source and destination node, max message length, priority, transmit mode, period, unique ID and data length. Data length is limited from 64 byes to max message length. They are major sent from each end system to end system 2,7 and 9. This is consider to the real avionic system, all of the sensors need transmit their message to control systems and databases.

The AFDX network could be initialized at the beginning 9 ms. At the instance t = 10ms, all VLs changed their data mode immediately. The virtual link could change their data length, priority and periods. After the instance, we make the network run 10 ms to make the network stable. We record the utilization of the network at the both mode. As well we work out the network transition time: in file old.txt, we write each VLs arrive time in mode one, and we get the network transition time through the last one of the arrive time subtract the mode change time t = 10ms.

div.head: B. Analysis
div.p: In Fig. 6, there is the transition time through simulations. When the network utilization is below 14.9%, no overload occure during the whole network transition. From the picture we can see, When we add the offset, the transitiom time is higher than before whenutilizition is below 14.9%. The result shows that, offset could make no message lose but the transition time is increased by a large margin.

Notice that when the transition time keeps at 0.98ms between the utilization is 14.9% and 18.7%. That because offset is feasible one, not an accurate one. In theory, the maximum of offset is the slot t m r . t m r is the slot from mode change occure to end of the all old mode message finish transmitting. The one we caculate here could satisfy the utilization between 14.9% and 18.7%. But it cause a big delay when utilization is 14.9%. Also we can predict the transtion time of the whole utilization is smaller than then T m r . And there will be a upper bound for the curve of the transtion time.

T ransition ≤ T m r T m r = max(t m r ), f or all utilization (10) When the utilization is below 14.9%, the transtion time of the network is not monotone. It shows that the transtion time do not follow the network utilization, but relative with the vls in AFDX network. From lots of the simulation we get the result: when the vls are centralized, the transtion time is higher than vls are disperse. One of the main causes is lots of vls flood into one output port of switch, the delay of schedule increases.

At last, we can conclude when no overload occurs, the transition time of the network is about below 1ms. When there is overload, our method could make no messages lose, and the transition time of the network is at about millisecond scale.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK
div.p: In this paper we presented a approach to solve the overload caused by mode change in AFDX network. An offset is introduced but the transition time could be increased. We can calculate the offset by the method of windows. In essence, the windows is calculate the worst case response time, it could guarantee the schedulability of the switch.

However, we cannot calculate the exact minimum offset. Through iteration we get an feasible value of offset. Then our next work is to calculate the range of the offset, make the transition time shorter than before.
